wind-chill-calculator.assumptionNote: The wind chill formula is valid only for air temperatures at or below 10°C (50°F) combined with wind speeds above 4.8 km/h (3 mph). Outside this range the number is shown for reference but is not a true wind chill.

faqs.a: Wind chill describes how cold the air feels on exposed skin when wind strips away the thin layer of warm air your body maintains. At 0°C with a 20 km/h wind, the air feels like minus 5.2°C. It is a feels-like temperature, not an actual temperature — your thermometer still reads 0°C.

The official formula (used by weather services in the US, Canada, and the UK) was developed from experiments on human volunteers in cold wind tunnels. It models heat loss from exposed skin. It is well validated inside its range: at or below 10°C with wind above 4.8 km/h. Outside that range it is meaningless.
faqs.q: Is the wind chill formula accurate?

faqs.a: Wind chill cannot go above the actual air temperature — if it feels warmer than the thermometer, that is humidity or sunshine, not wind chill. Also, wind chill applies to exposed skin, so it does not tell you how fast a car radiator or a water pipe will cool.
faqs.q: Can wind chill be warmer than the air temperature?

faqs.a: Cover exposed skin: balaclava or scarf, insulated gloves, and windproof outer layers. The risk badge on this page follows Environment Canada guidance: below minus 28°C, exposed skin can freeze within 30 minutes; below minus 40°C, within 10 minutes. Keep trips short and check on other people.
faqs.q: How do I stay safe when wind chill is very low?

faqs.a: No. Wind chill is only defined for cold conditions. For hot weather, weather services use the heat index, which combines temperature and humidity to estimate how hot it feels. JaurTools plans a heat index calculator as a companion tool.
faqs.q: Is there a summer version of wind chill?

faqs.a: Because your body heats a thin boundary layer of air next to your skin, and wind constantly replaces it with cold air. The faster the wind, the faster heat is carried away, so your skin cools toward the wind chill value rather than the still-air temperature.
faqs.q: Why does wind make cold feel colder?

wind-chill-calculator.formula:
Wind chill (°C) = 13.12 + 0.6215 × T − 11.37 × V^0.16 + 0.3965 × T × V^0.16
T = air temperature in °C, V = wind speed in km/h.
Valid only when T ≤ 10°C and V ≥ 4.8 km/h.
howTo: Pick your temperature unit: Celsius or Fahrenheit.
Enter the air temperature from your thermometer or forecast.
Pick your wind-speed unit: km/h or mph.
Enter the wind speed. Use the sustained wind, not gusts, for the standard value.
Read the feels-like temperature and the frostbite-risk badge instantly.
keyFacts: Wind chill is the feels-like temperature on exposed skin in wind and cold.
The standard formula comes from US and Canadian weather services.
At 0°C with a 20 km/h wind, it feels like minus 5.2°C.
The formula is only valid at or below 10°C with wind above 4.8 km/h.
Below minus 28°C wind chill, exposed skin can freeze within 30 minutes.
Wind chill never applies to objects — only to living, heat-producing skin.
